extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for determining eligibility, filing, and processing of patent term extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. 156 and related USPTO implementing regulations (37 CFR §§1.710–1.740). Covers what constitutes a "product," timing, contents, signatures, and special-case rules (e.g., animal drugs, recombinant manufacturing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver conditions for recalculation filing-window requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to file a request for recalculation of patent term adjustment within two months of the patent issuance and include information required by 37 CFR 1.705(b)(2) and fee required by 37 CFR 1.18(e) were sua sponte waived for patents that met all of the following criteria: (1) The patent issued between January 14, 2013 and May 20, 2014; (2) the patent resulted directly from an international application that has entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; and (3) the Request for Recalculation of the Patent Term Adjustment form (PTO/SB/132) was filed no later than July 31, 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.183. This waiver does not apply to patents issued on or after May 20, 2014, and does not apply to requests that the Office recalculate the patent term adjustment for alleged errors other than the above-identified errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional procedure is a new PTA determination, not a reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for recalculation of patent term adjustment under the optional procedure is not a request for reconsideration within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3), and a recalculation under the optional procedure is not the Director's decision on an applicant's request for reconsideration within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3) and (b)(4). Rather, it is simply a new patent term adjustment determination under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for reconsideration of a new PTA determination resulting from the recalculation must comply with 37 CFR 1.705(b)(1) and (b)(2) and be filed no later than two months from the date of the new PTA determination. That two-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's exclusive civil-action remedy preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the optional procedure shall be construed as a waiver of the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4) that an applicant dissatisfied with the Director's decision on the applicant's request for reconsideration under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3)(B)(ii) shall have exclusive remedy by a civil action against the Director filed in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days after the date of the Director's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory scope of 35 U.S.C. 156: what patents can be extended
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent which claims a product, a method of using a product, or a method of manufacturing a product shall be extended in accordance with this section from the original expiration date of the patent (including any PTA under 154(b)) if statutory conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 156 defines eligibility and extension rights (see subsections (a) and (b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility condition — patent must not have expired before extension application filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of the patent has not expired before an application is submitted under subsection (d)(1) for its extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include applications for interim extension under subsection (d)(5). See MPEP explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility condition — no previous extension under subsection (e)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of the patent has never been extended under subsection (e)(1) of 35 U.S.C. 156 (with limited exceptions per regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.720(b) explains that extension is available only if the patent term has never been previously extended, except for extensions issued pursuant to 37 CFR 1.701, 1.760, or 1.790 (administrative or interim extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility condition — application submitted by owner of record or agent and in compliance with subsection (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for extension must be submitted by the owner of record of the patent or its agent and in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs (1) through (4) of subsection (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.730 requires submission by owner of record or agent and specifies signature requirements (owner signature or registered practitioner; agents require registered practitioner signature and proof of authorization on request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility condition — product subject to regulatory review period before commercial marketing or use
rubrics_metrics.description: The product has been subject to a regulatory review period before its commercial marketing or use as defined in 35 U.S.C. 156(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory review must be the type defined by statute; e.g., a 510(k) review is not a qualifying regulatory review period. For medical devices, review must have occurred under section 515, not section 505.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility condition — approval must be first permitted commercial marketing or use
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in statutory exceptions, the permission for commercial marketing or use of the product after the regulatory review period must be the first permitted commercial marketing or use of the product under the law under which such regulatory review occurred (35 U.S.C. 156(a)(5)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include (B) for patents claiming a method of manufacturing a product primarily using recombinant DNA technology (first permitted marketing or use of a product manufactured under the claimed process), and (C) special rules for new animal drugs/veterinary biological products (see statutory text and 37 CFR 1.720(e)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "product" under 35 U.S.C. 156(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "product" means: (A) The active ingredient of a new human drug, antibiotic drug, or human biological product (including any salt or ester of the active ingredient, as a single entity or in combination); (B) The active ingredient of a new animal drug or veterinary biological product (that is not primarily manufactured using recombinant DNA/RNA, hybridoma, or site-specific genetic manipulation), including any salt or ester; or (C) Any medical device, food additive, or color additive subject to regulation under the FD&C Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 21 CFR 60.3(b) for definitions of active ingredient and related terms. Animal biological products are approved by USDA (Plant and Animal Inspection Service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of "drug product" (active ingredient present in final dosage form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A "drug product" means the active ingredient found in the final dosage form prior to administration of the product to the patient, not the resultant form the drug may take after administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility turns on whether the active ingredient present in the final dosage form was previously approved; different salts/esters can be different drug products (e.g., ester vs. salt). Case law examples cited (PhotoCure; Glaxo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple active ingredients: basis for extension if any one active ingredient was previously unapproved
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a product contains multiple active ingredients, if any one active ingredient has not been previously approved, it can form the basis of an extension for that ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A different ratio of hormones is not a different active ingredient. An approved product with two active ingredients will not be considered a single active ingredient made of the two. See In re Alcon Laboratories and Arnold Partnership v. Dudas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enantiomer rule: enantiomer can be distinct product
rubrics_metrics.description: An enantiomer may be considered a separate drug product from the racemate and each can support patent term extension, despite prior approval of the racemate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case: Ortho-McNeil Pharmaceutical Inc. v. Lupin Pharmaceuticals Inc., 603 F.3d 1377.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one patent may be extended per regulatory review period; election required if multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one application for patent term extension is filed based upon a single regulatory review period, an election will be required of a single patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2761 for examples and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminally disclaimed patents may be eligible for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be extended under 35 U.S.C. 156 even though it has been terminally disclaimed; PTE is a limited extension attached to the original patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2) precludes adjustment for patents terminally disclaimed due to obviousness-type double patenting, 35 U.S.C. 156 contains no such exclusion. See Merck & Co. v. Hi‑Tech Pharmacal (Fed. Cir. 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.720 — conditions for extension (regulatory restatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent may be extended if: (a) the patent claims a product as defined in §1.710; (b) the term has never been previously extended (with noted exceptions); (c) an application is submitted in compliance with §1.740; (d) the product has been subject to a regulatory review period as defined in 35 U.S.C. 156(g) before its commercial marketing or use; (e) the product has received permission for commercial marketing or use and meets the 'first permitted marketing' conditions (with exceptions); (f) the application is submitted within the sixty-day period beginning on the date the product first received permission; (g) the patent term has not expired before submission; and (h) no other patent has been extended for the same regulatory review period for the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This summarizes statutory and regulatory prerequisites; see MPEP narrative and statutory text for details and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.710 — definition of product and drug product for PTE
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is eligible if it claims a 'product' as defined (drug product, medical device, food/color additive) either alone or in combination, or a method of using/manufacturing such product. 'Drug product' means the active ingredient of a new human/animal drug or biological product, excluding animal drugs primarily manufactured using recombinant DNA/RNA/hybridoma/site-specific genetic techniques, and includes salts/esters as single entities or in combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also defines 'major health or environmental effects test' (test reasonably related to evaluation of health/environmental effects that requires at least six months to conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.730 & signature requirements for PTE application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application for extension must be submitted by the owner of record or its agent and comply with §1.740. If submitted by the patent owner, it must be signed either by the patent owner in compliance with §3.73(b) or by a registered practitioner on behalf of the owner. If submitted by an agent (e.g., licensee), it must be signed by a registered practitioner on behalf of the agent. The Office may require proof that the agent/practitioner is authorized to act on behalf of the patent owner or agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may request proof of authorization if the application is signed by a registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1) — required application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain extension under this section, the owner of record or agent shall submit an application within the 60-day period; the application shall contain: (A) identity of the approved product and the Federal statute under which regulatory review occurred; (B) identity of the patent and identity of each claim which claims the approved product or method of using/manufacturing it; (C) information to enable Director to determine eligibility and rights and to enable Secretary of HHS or Agriculture to determine the period of extension; (D) a brief description of the activities undertaken by the applicant during the regulatory review period and significant dates; and (E) such patent or other information as the Director may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of determining the date a product receives permission, transmissions after 4:30 P.M. Eastern or transmissions on non-business days are deemed received the next business day. 'Business day' is defined as Mon–Fri excluding federal holidays under 5 U.S.C. 6103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered-date special rule for controlled-substance or similar cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of subsection (i), if HHS provides notice that it intends to recommend controls under the Controlled Substances Act beginning on the covered date, the drug product shall be considered to have been approved/indexed and have permission for commercial marketing or use beginning on the covered date. The 'covered date' is the later of specified approval/indexing dates under various statutory sections or issuance of an interim final rule under CSA section 201(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection (i) provides particular rules for controlled-substance scheduling contexts and related timing for the 60-day filing period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency relationship required when applicant is not the marketing applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant for patent term extension was not the marketing applicant before the regulatory agency, there must be an agency relationship between the patent owner and the marketing applicant during the regulatory review period to rely upon the marketing applicant's activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is advisable for the PTE applicant to obtain a letter from the marketing applicant specifically authorizing such reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory-review ineligibility examples (510(k), section 505 vs 515)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory review period under section 510(k) is not a regulatory review period that gives rise to eligibility for patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156. If the product is alleged to be a medical device, regulatory review must have occurred under section 515 (not section 505).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case references: In re Nitinol Medical Technologies (510(k) not eligible); Baxter Diagnostics v. AVL Scientific (Class III devices intended).
